ACLS through the American Heart Association (AHA)
Bachelors Of Science in Nursing (BSN) or equivalent combination of education and experience
Five (5) years of professional clinical experience in critical care or
One (1) year of experience caring for Ventricular Assist Device patients
One (1) year of experience as a VAD Coordinator

Manages the care of the high-risk ventricular assist device (VAD) patient population across the continuum (acute care inpatient, within the home, physician office, VAD Clinic, and extended care facilities) in collaboration with the Medical Director, cardiac surgeons, cardiologists, and other members of the multidisciplinary team. This involves advanced assessment, planning and coordination of care, modification of the treatment plans indicated and the monitoring and evaluation of outcomes.

In conjunction with physicians and program director, program development may include but is not limited to: Outpatient clinical care forms, patient and physician professional communication tools, clinical care protocols, policy and procedures VAD patient data tracking methodology (using 4D)

Coordinates the referral, screening, additional patient testing requirements, consult appointments and hospital-based procedures. Provides clinical consultation and education related to the management and care of the complex cardiac surgical patient and VAD devices for staff, physicians, as well as other disciplines that may have contact or care responsibilities for this population.
In collaboration with the Medical Director, designs and oversees performance improvement activities associated the VAD patients to improve patient outcomes

Develops a therapeutic relationship with the VAD patients and family and maximizes the patient's participation and control in their own recovery. Facilitates the access and utilization of community resources and organizations to assist in the patient's recovery.
1.6Oversees and provides education to acute care staff (ED, CVOR, CVICU and PCU).
